proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV) insulating phosphate that is electrochemically robust at about 4 V and chemically compatible with the PS4 3- framework of Li6PS5Cl, so it should give a low interfacial penalty. LiCl is a wide-gap, insulating halide. Its Cl- anion matches the Cl- in Li6PS5Cl, so it should be chemically compatible with the electrolyte and avoid the P-S-O type reactions seen with Li3PO4. It is also a chemically different family from the phosphate tested so far.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) was insulating and wide-gap but gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16, not acceptable), with reaction products P2O5, SCl4, and SO2. A halide coating may reduce this interfacial reactivity.

Fluoride should resist the P-S and Cl reactions that produced SCl4, PCl5, and P2O5 with Li3PO4 and LiCl.
